title: Kth Smallest Element in a Sorted Matrix
prompt: Given an `n x n` matrix `matrix` where each row and each column is sorted in ascending order, return the k-th smallest element in the matrix (counted as the k-th smallest in sorted order across the entire matrix, not the k-th distinct element).

examples.explanation: The sorted order of the matrix elements is [1,5,9,10,11,12,13,13,15], and the 8th smallest is 13.

constraints: each row and column of matrix is sorted in ascending order
hints: Merging all n sorted rows into one sorted list and indexing into it works but costs O(n^2 log n) or more.

Instead of searching positions, binary search on the value itself: pick a candidate value and count how many matrix elements are <= it, which can be done in O(n) using the sorted-rows-and-columns structure (like a staircase walk from the bottom-left).
That count is monotonically non-decreasing as the candidate value increases, so binary search the value range [matrix[0][0], matrix[n-1][n-1]] for the smallest value whose count is >= k.

solution.approach: Binary search on the value range between the matrix's minimum and maximum elements rather than on positions. For a candidate value, count how many matrix elements are less than or equal to it in O(n) time by walking from the bottom-left corner: move right while the current cell is <= the candidate (adding all elements above it in that column), and move up otherwise. This count is monotonically non-decreasing in the candidate value, so binary search for the smallest value whose count is at least k, which is guaranteed to be an actual matrix element and thus the k-th smallest.
